answer: Sure, here's a shorter version: The sky is blue because of Rayleigh scattering. Air molecules are much smaller than the wavelength of light, so they scatter short blue wavelengths much more strongly than long red ones, and that blue light reaches us from every part of the sky [1][2]. Violet light scatters even more, but the Sun gives off less of it and our eyes are less sensitive to it [2]. At sunrise and sunset, sunlight passes through more air, so most of the blue is scattered away and the sky near the Sun looks orange and red [1].
